Fjord Fuzz MIDGARD
sources.excerpt: Fjord Fuzz MIDGARD Electric Guitars Berly Duesenberg Ernie Ball Gavilan Jet Knaggs Luxxtone Nash Nik Huber Novo Rock N Roll Relics Suhr Tausch Yamaha Preowned Acoustic Guitars Alvarez Yamaha Amps Amplified Nation Carr Suhr Used/Vintage Pedals Cornerstone Effects Fjord Fuzz Greer Pedals Vemuram Preowned Pedals Accessories Cables Guitar Straps Pickups Contact Pedals > Fjord Fuzz MIDGARD Fjord Fuzz MIDGARD SKU: $199.00 $199.00 Unavailable per item MIDGARD uses a traditional, but very lovely classic BC108 fuzz circuit, but expands on the theme with a few very unique features. Similar to many fuzzes before it, MIDGARD let’s you add a buffer and a pickup simulator in front of the fuzz circuit itself. This makes it so that the fuzz no longer cares about whatever you might stick in front of it, but unlike other pedals like it, MIDGARD has a fully separate input jack just for this feature. In other words, you can bypass it completely if you don’t need it for your purposes, but more importantly, this input circuit is an always-on feature on the secondary jack. The bypass switch only toggles the fuzz circuit. This means the pedal can also offer the same input correction to any of your other finicky fuzzes. It also means you can use the included fuzz, or any other fuzz, or even any other guitar electronics, even amps, with whatever instrument you might please. You could even use it as a dedicated reamplification device, to send whatever tracks you want from your audio interface through MIDGARD and into any of your pedals and amps. The buffer itself is using an OPA1656 chip both for the audio buffering, and also for its power handling, for a truly exquisite input behaviour, normally only seen in high end studio equipment. MIDGARD also comes with an expression pedal jack input which allows you to get that classic fuzz cleanup, no matter where you stick it in your audio chain. sources.excerpt: New Pedal: Fjord Fuzz Midgard | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit New Pedal: Fjord Fuzz Midgard Updated Jul. 7, 2026  |  by Brent P. Gladless Most fuzz pedals do one thing. The Fjord Fuzz Midgard does two, and the second one is the reason to buy it. The fuzz side is solid — warm, thick, not harsh. You can plug straight in and get there. Or you can hit the preamp first: a Texas Instruments op-amp that’s clean as bottled water, then shove that signal through a beat-up old transformer choke from a ’57 Musicmaster. Clean preamp into dirty iron. It’s a weird recipe that lands exactly right. But the Translator is the thing. Kill the fuzz, leave the Translator on, and your whole pedalboard stops caring what you plug into it. Synths. Drum machines. Laptops. That old tape deck you keep meaning to fix. The Translator sorts out impedance and signal level so your pedals behave the same way they do with a guitar — which means every drive, delay, and weird modulation you own just became usable with anything that makes noise. Add a volume pedal anywhere in the chain and you get that cleanup tone — the one where rolling back turns a roar into a purr — on any instrument, not just a guitar. Two circuits that work together or apart. Not flashy. Just useful in ways you won’t realize until you’ve had it on your board for a month.
